sn22.54:1.2: These terms are defined in detail in [pli-tv-bu-vb-pc11:2.1.1](). _Bījajāta_ are not “kinds of seeds” but “that which is born from a seed” i.e. “plants” (_bhūtagāmo nāma pañca bījajātāni_).
sn22.54:1.4: “Plants propagated from roots” (_mūlabīja_, literally “that which has a root for a seed”) include ginger and turmeric; from “stems” (_khandhabīja_) the Bodhi tree and the banyan tree; from “cuttings” (_aggabīja_) basil and hemp; from “joints” (_phalubīja_) sugarcane and bamboo; and from “regular seeds” (_bījabīja_), grains and vegetables.
sn22.54:1.5: _Sukhasayita_ is sometimes understood as “well planted”, but how can it be planted when there is no soil? It is explained by the commentary as “well-kept”, literally “well laid by”.
sn22.54:1.11: Pali uses the same word _viññāṇaṭṭhiti_ for the seven “planes of consciousness” (realms of rebirth, [an7.44](), [dn15:33.1]()) as for the four “grounds for consciousness”, the other four aggregates on which consciousness is based.
sn22.54:1.13: See too [an3.76:2.3](): “deeds are the field, consciousness is the seed, and craving is the moisture”.
sn22.54:4.2: For the “establishment of consciousness”, namely the rebirth of consciousness in a new life, see too [sn12.64]().
